display.title: Tanya Shiur 42: Ahavas Yisroel, Tanya Chapter 32
display.summary_short: A Yiddish Tanya shiur on chapter 32: why every Jew is truly a brother, how love for a fellow Jew is the whole Torah, and how to love even someone whose deeds you must reject.
display.summary_long: Shiur 42 in Rabbi Yosef Goldstein's Yiddish Tanya series covers all of chapter 32, which he calls the heart of the Tanya. All souls come from one root, like twins with one Father; only the body divides them, like a passing cloud that hides the sun. That is why Hillel called Ahavas Yisroel the whole Torah. He explains that the Shechinah rests only where Jews are united: 'Bless us, our Father, all of us as one'; a Sefer Torah missing a single letter is unfit; the Torah could not have been given if even one Jew were missing at Sinai. He cites the Baal Shem Tov's teaching that a soul may come down for seventy or eighty years just to do another Jew one favor, and links the Rebbe's Ahavas Yisroel campaign to bringing Moshiach for every Jew. Yaakov's ladder becomes a picture of davening, which begins by accepting the mitzvah to love one's fellow. A story tells of a Chabad Rebbe whose few words in a tavern brought a lost Jew back. The second half explains the Gemara's 'mitzvah to hate' a sinner: hate only the evil, love the G-dly spark, and let compassion dissolve the hatred, like the students of Aharon who loved peace and drew people close to Torah.
display.lesson: Every Jew is part of one soul with you: love him for his G-dly spark, bring him close with warmth, and let compassion overcome any dislike of his deeds.

study_text.note: Whole chapter, from the opening on body and soul to the end (Dovid HaMelech's 'perfect hatred').

segments.title: Tanya 32: one root for all souls
segments.summary: Body divides, soul unites: the cloud and the sun, Hillel's 'whole Torah', and why the Shechinah rests only on unity.

segments.title: One letter, one Jew
segments.summary: A Sefer Torah missing one letter is unfit, and the Torah could not be given if one Jew were missing at Sinai.

segments.title: The Baal Shem Tov: a lifetime for one favor
segments.summary: A soul may come down for seventy or eighty years just to do one Jew a favor.

segments.title: Ahavas Yisroel and the coming of Moshiach
segments.summary: The Rebbe's Ahavas Yisroel campaign: Moshiach redeems every Jew, so we must reach every Jew and take the galus out of him.

segments.title: Yaakov's ladder and davening
segments.summary: Prayer is the ladder joining heaven and earth, climbed through four worlds, and one climbs it whole by first accepting the mitzvah to love every Jew.

segments.title: A Rebbe in the tavern
segments.summary: A few holy words from a Chabad Rebbe traveling incognito stir a lost Jew to come back (a story the Rebbe told).

segments.title: Lighting the candle
segments.summary: Bring a distant Jew into warmth and he lights up by himself; the time is short, so share Chassidus right away.

segments.title: Three meanings of 'arevim'
segments.summary: Jews are responsible for, mixed with and sweet to one another, and a Father's greatest joy is his children's love.

segments.title: Tanya 32: loving one whose deeds you reject
segments.summary: The Gemara's 'mitzvah to hate' a sinner applies narrowly; hate the evil, love the G-dly spark, and compassion dissolves the hatred.

segments.title: Aharon makes peace
segments.summary: Aharon tells each of two quarreling men that the other is sorry, until they make up.

segments.title: The heart of the Tanya
segments.summary: Chapter 32 is the 'lev' of the Tanya; a prayer to greet Moshiach soon with the Tanya in hand.
